teams.heading: Fijisun reports White in contention for Flying Fijians head coach role
teams.body: Fijisun has reported that White is in contention for the Flying Fijians coaching role, while Planet Rugby reported earlier this month that an ex-Springboks boss was the favourite to land the job ahead of the 2027 Rugby World Cup. Fiji have been looking for a successor since Mick Byrne left by mutual agreement on 1 April, and no appointment has been reported in coverage up to today. The next Test is France in Round 4, with the appointment still open.

teams.heading: PREM: England winger Immanuel Feyi-Waboso awaits hamstring scan after Exeter win
teams.body: In the PREM, England winger Immanuel Feyi-Waboso awaits scans on a possible hamstring injury after leaving Exeter's 34-28 win over Newcastle Red Bulls on Sunday 11 October early in the second half. Exeter director of rugby Rob Baxter said the winger "just doesn’t feel right", adding that it was not "catastrophic". Exeter open their Investec Champions Cup campaign at Toulouse, and Feyi-Waboso has already missed time this year, including the 2026 Six Nations.

lead.why: A new England injury worry for a key winger ahead of the November Tests, and the pack's most concrete fresh news.

teams.heading: Stade Français hooker Lucas Peyresblanques fractures fibula in Top 14 win
teams.body: Stade Français, the Top 14 club, face their opening Investec Champions Cup match against the Bulls at Loftus Versfeld with three injury setbacks. The most serious is hooker Lucas Peyresblanques, who fractured his fibula in the 30-22 win over Montpellier and underwent surgery on Sunday. Coach Paul Gustard said: "We risk losing him for five to six months." No. 8 Yoan Tanga left after nine minutes with a rib injury, and centre Noah Nene, who hurt his right ankle, could be sidelined for around two weeks.

lead.why: It is the only new item on the shortlist, and it is a France-based injury story with a named player and a coach quote.

teams.heading: Brain injury claimants face £2.8m bill to keep legal action alive
teams.body: No development has been reported since the Guardian reported on 10 October that rugby's brain injury claimants face a £2.8m legal bill to continue their case. The claim carries a £2.8m funding deadline, and no revised timetable, settlement or stay of proceedings has been reported since. Today's coverage carries nothing further on the case against the rugby governing bodies, so the last confirmed position is the 10 October report.

teams.heading: Scotland lost 25-17 at home to New Zealand in November 2025
teams.body: Scotland's last meeting with New Zealand ended in a 25-17 home defeat in November 2025, an International Friendlies match. Scotland sit fifth of 12 in the log after three matches, with two wins and one defeat. Points for stand at 108 and points against at 97. Their last result was a 33-17 win over Fiji in Round three. Scotland's next match is against New Zealand in Round four of the Nations Championship.

teams.heading: Wales Online's Steffan Thomas says Taine Basham should be picked
teams.body: Steve Tandy will name his Wales squad for the second instalment of the Nations Championship in the coming days, and Wales Online's Steffan Thomas argues Taine Basham has made an undeniable case for inclusion. The 26-year-old, whose last of 17 caps came against England in 2024, has excelled at No 8 for Cardiff since his summer 2025 move from the Dragons, and his discipline has improved markedly. Even in last Saturday's comfortable defeat by Leinster, he stood out against a side packed with British & Irish Lions.

teams.heading: Tom Wright says Wallabies are 'chomping at the bit' for Sydney rematch
teams.body: Full-back Tom Wright says the Wallabies are 'chomping at the bit' for next Saturday's rematch at Accor Stadium, having faced the music after the 50-19 loss at Eden Park. Wright conceded the aerial and kicking battle went the All Blacks' way, and that Australia were 'right in the contest' at 17-14 before the second half slipped away. Assistant coach Donnelly says Len Ikitau has a concussion and Jordan Petaia is also heading home, with the rest of the squad carrying only bumps and bruises.

lead.why: The strongest new item, with fresh Wallabies voice on the review and an injury update the earlier editions did not carry.

teams.heading: Japan suspend Eddie Jones for four games over abuse of match officials
teams.body: In May, the JRFU suspended head coach Eddie Jones for four games and cut his salary over 'verbal abuse directed at local officials' during the Japan U23s' tour of Australia in April. Jones accepted the decision. The suspension ran from 24 April to 5 June and also ruled him out of the Japan XV match against the Maori All Blacks in Nagoya on 27 June, as well as the Nations Championship opener against Italy in Tokyo on 4 July.

lead.why: The only men's senior story in the pack involving a Japan figure, and it is dated plainly as a May ruling.

teams.heading: Beauden Barrett admits omission challenged him mentally before Bledisloe full-back return
teams.body: Beauden Barrett has said being left out of most of the All Blacks' Test matches this year challenged him mentally. The 35-year-old missed the Springbok Tests in South Africa and the July Nations Championship games, and said: "It did challenge me mentally a little bit with not being selected and just feeling a little bit off the pace." He returned at full-back in last Saturday's 50-19 Bledisloe Cup win over Australia at Eden Park.

lead.why: A personal storyline from a senior All Black returning to the Test side, with a direct quote and a fresh angle beyond last Saturday's result.

teams.heading: URC: Sharks reportedly join Bulls in chase for Springbok Malcolm Marx
teams.body: Malcolm Marx is attracting URC interest again, with the Sharks reportedly entering the race to sign the Springbok when his Kubota Spears contract expires midway through 2027, according to Rapport. The Bulls have been pursuing the 32-year-old for a couple of months, and a source told Rapport that Pietersen, Dave Williams and Ruan Jacobs have met to discuss a move. The Sharks' interest is tied to Bongi Mbonambi's uncertain position, with the 35-year-old awaiting a Sharks disciplinary hearing after missing the opening three URC games.

lead.why: A new report on a current Springbok's future, with a Bulls-Sharks contest and a live Mbonambi angle, is the story a fan would text a mate about.
